from.place: Proof paragraph 2, finite coefficient mapping-complex adjunction before R lim: enriched tensor cocontinuity foundation; Haugseng Observation 3.9; Gepner-Haugseng, Enriched infinity-categories via nonsymmetric infinity-operads, Proposition 3.6.10 and section 4.3 (in particular Proposition 4.3.14)

title: Cocontinuous unary change of enrichment on algebroids
statement:
Let $V,W$ be cocomplete monoidal infinity categories whose tensors preserve small colimits separately, with algebroids as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. The infinity categories $\operatorname{Algd}(V)$ and $\operatorname{Algd}(W)$ admit small colimits. If $F:V\to W$ is strong monoidal and preserves small colimits, composition of operadic algebras with $F$ defines $F_*:\operatorname{Algd}(V)\to\operatorname{Algd}(W)$, and this functor preserves small colimits. Explicitly, for every small infinity category $K$ and diagram $A:K\to\operatorname{Algd}(V)$, the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}F_*A_k\longrightarrow F_*(\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}A_k)$$
is an equivalence. This includes the empty diagram. No presentability hypothesis on $V,W$ is assumed.

source.place: Observation 3.9; Gepner-Haugseng, Enriched infinity-categories via nonsymmetric infinity-operads, Proposition 3.6.10 and section 4.3 (in particular Proposition 4.3.14); online source, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Use the object-space projection $p_{\mathcal V}:\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)\to\mathcal S$ of [lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration], which is a Cartesian (hence inner) fibration for any monoidal $\mathcal V$. Its fiber is $\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$, and its mapping-space homotopy fiber over $f:X\to Y$ is $\operatorname{Map}(A,f^*B)$. The same cited statement constructs postcomposition by $F$ as a functor $F_*$ over $\mathcal S$ commuting coherently with restriction. Thus its object space is unchanged and its fiber functor $H_X$ is postcomposition on algebras. No cocontinuity assertion is being taken from this node.

source.place: Definitions 3.6.1, 3.6.12 and 4.3.1; Lemma 4.3.9. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Put $q(X)=L_{\mathrm{gen}}\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$. The natural equivalence of [lem-coef-many-object-operad-accessibility] identifies $\operatorname{Alg}_{q(X)}(\mathcal V)$ with $\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$, for every monoidal $\mathcal V$. It commutes with restriction in $X$ and postcomposition in $\mathcal V$: both are composition with the same unit $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to q(X)$. Each $q(X)$ is a small ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad; by the Segal condition at $[0]$ in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], its zero-fiber is contractible. Consequently for every $f:X\to Y$, $q(f)$ is an equivalence on zero-fibers and satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-coef-operadic-cocomplete-extensions]. Apply that node to $q(f)$, and transport its adjunction along these natural equivalences, obtaining $f_!^{\mathcal V}\dashv f^*$. Also [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-colimit-change] applied to $q(X)$ gives all small fiber colimits, and says that each $H_X$ preserves them. These applications use only cocompleteness and separate tensor cocontinuity, not presentability. We use $q(f)$ here, not $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta_Y^{\mathrm{op}}$, whose zero-fiber map need not be an equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.14; Remark 4.3.2; Theorem A.4.6; Corollary A.5.7; Proposition A.5.10. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-left-adjoint-transport] to the Cartesian object-space projections of step 1 and the adjoints $f_!^{\mathcal V}\dashv f^*$ of step 2. Its hypotheses hold for every map $f:X\to Y$ of small spaces, without presentability. Both object-space projections are therefore cocartesian fibrations. Their covariant transports are the free extensions $f_!^{\mathcal V}$ and $f_!^{\mathcal W}$, and the specified adjunction units give cocartesian arrows $A\to f_!^{\mathcal V}A$ and $B\to f_!^{\mathcal W}B$ in the respective total categories. The cited unit clause supplies the precise lifts needed for the coefficient-change mate in step 6.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.6 and Lemma 4.3.7; Cartesian-to-cocartesian criterion made explicit in Kerodon Proposition 6.2.5.7 (02FP). Online source read; archive WANTED.

proof.text:
The transports preserve colimits by the following three-equivalence calculation. Let $B:K\to\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$ be small and $\ell=\operatorname{colim}B$, which exists by [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-colimit-change]. The adjunction of [lem-coef-operadic-cocomplete-extensions], the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and the dual coherent-diagram adjunction of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] give, for every $C$,
$$\operatorname{Map}(f_!\ell,C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(\ell,f^*C)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Alg}_X)}(B,\operatorname{const}(f^*C))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Alg}_Y)}(f_!B,\operatorname{const}(C)).$$
The first and last equivalences are adjunct maps; the middle map is precomposition with the colimit cocone. Their composite is precomposition with its image cocone, by the naturality of the adjunction unit. The same cocone criterion proves that image cocone colimiting. The calculation applies also to $\mathcal W$ and to empty $K$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.3.7, the phrase that transports preserve colimits being left adjoints; expanded directly from the cited coherent-adjunction and cocone mapping-space formulas.

proof.text: The base $\mathcal S$ admits all small colimits: [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback] states that spaces are presentable and every presentable infinity category has small colimits. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-grothendieck-limits-colimits] to the cocartesian fibrations of steps 3-4 and the cocomplete fibers of step 2. This proves both total categories are cocomplete and gives the actual colimit cocones. More explicitly, for the given small $K$-diagram $A$, put $X=\operatorname{colim}_K X_k$ with cocone $f_k:X_k\to X$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to its coherent base transformation to the constant diagram at $X$. The resulting transported diagram $D$ lies in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V))$, with $D_k=f_{k,!}^{\mathcal V}A_k$ and a coherent cocartesian transformation $A\to D$. Thus it is a coherent diagram, not just the list of transported objects. The total-colimit formula says that $L=\operatorname{colim}^{\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)}_K D$ equipped with the composite cocone from $A$ is a colimit of $A$ in $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.9 and Lemma 4.3.7; the cocartesian total-category colimit formula used there. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text:
For every $f:X\to Y$, apply the coefficient-change mate of [lem-coef-operadic-cocomplete-extensions] to $q(f)$, as justified in step 2. It yields a natural equivalence
$$f_!^{\mathcal W}H_X\xrightarrow{\sim}H_Yf_!^{\mathcal V}.$$
Its defining unit formula says that the image under $F_*$ of the cocartesian unit arrow $A\to f_!^{\mathcal V}A$ is the $\mathcal W$-cocartesian unit arrow $H_XA\to f_!^{\mathcal W}H_XA$ followed by this equivalence in the fiber over $Y$. It is therefore cocartesian: precomposition by a fiber equivalence leaves the mapping-space pullback criterion unchanged. Any other cocartesian lift over $f$ with the same source has the same mapping-space universal property: the two properties give maps between the targets over the identity of $Y$, and their composites are homotopic to the respective identities by uniqueness in those mapping-space fibers. Hence their targets are equivalent in the fiber. It follows that $F_*$ preserves all cocartesian arrows. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to the transformation $A\to D$ from step 5. Its image $F_*A\to H_XD$ has cocartesian components, and hence is a cocartesian lift of the same coherent base transformation. The cited node's coherent transport and mapping-space formula identify the transported diagram for $F_*A$ with $H_XD$, including its cocone from $F_*A$. Thus the equivalences here identify transformations and their higher simplices, not just object values.

source.place: Lemma A.4.7 and the proof of Proposition 3.6.10. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-colimit-change], the fiber functor $H_X$ preserves the $K$-colimit of $D$; hence the canonical fiber comparison $\operatorname{colim}^{\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal W)}_K H_XD\to H_XL$ is an equivalence compatible with the fiber cocone. The formula of [lem-coef-infinity-grothendieck-limits-colimits], using the coherent transported diagram identified in step 6, identifies its source with $\operatorname{colim}_K F_*A$. Its target, regarded in the total category over $X$, is $F_*L$. The compatibility with the transported cocones shows that this arrow is precisely the canonical comparison in the item. For $K$ empty the base colimit is $X=\varnothing$, the transported diagram is empty, and the same fiber theorem sends its initial object to the initial object in the fiber over $\varnothing$. The total-colimit formula then makes the comparison an equivalence for the empty diagram too. This proves every asserted colimit preservation statement under the original hypotheses.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.10; Proposition A.5.10; the same fiber argument as Lemma 4.3.7. Read online; agent reconstruction, archive WANTED.
